Not urgent and more for my knowledge, not a feedback point - do we actually successfully abide by a 24h SLA for getting users an analysis back after they report?  Asking as it could become a point of user dissatisfaction if we can't live up to this promise - and we should avoid making promises we can't keep in the messaging if we currently do not.

The reduced focus is much better! 

IMO We should move this to be more secondary to the letter grade (potentially below the letter grade in position?) so that we can deliver them the value of the rating first, then give the user agency to decide if they want to update for something newer. 

Thinking that having a CTA at the very top is like asking the user right away to do some work for us (click the Refresh button) before we give them something of value - we ought to flip flop that, since we don't necessarily want to drive them to reanalyze as a primary CTA if they can get value out of the existing rating.

* I think the user's job to be done here is "run review checker" so I'd put the CTA above the image
* Given above, I'd also reduce image size/complexity or remove altogether. This is clever, but takes a while to grok and seems irrevelant and makes the job to be done harder

I wonder if it would help to have the body text "do the work" (e.g. mention smth along the lines of "Would you like to report this product back in stock")  and the button be more laconic (e.g.: "Report back in stock" or just "Report"?)

Warning: Incoming random thoughts about .. small details. Take with a grain of salt.. :grimacing:

Do users have enough context to know what this is refreshing? Is refresh the right verb? Could refresh be conflated with browser refresh? Is Coke Zero a superior calorie-free beverage compared to Diet Coke?

Seriously though, could this be an opportunity to use language that makes me feel more empowered? Re-analyzing made it feel like I initiated real work, for example.

Since we don't know yet how often we'll run across this scenario, and my uninformed guess is that this refresh message could show up a lot in our first versions, I'm a little worried about this creating a jumpy experience with the card/message showing up and disappearing. Could we consider giving his component a space to live that doesn't push down all of the content of the sidebar?

:thought_balloon: Do we even need this confirmation? Once I have new info, just show it to me. Don't give me something to have to manage / dismiss / etc. Same model as refreshing a webpage .. the confirmation is in the updated information. If we're concerned about a perception of "stale" info, we could put a "last updated" timestamp somewhere.
